answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks by enforcing verifiable delay functions at its ingress wharf, admitting peers to the operational haven only upon receiving non-parallelizable mathematical proofs. An attacker incurs an unavoidable physical time and ASIC hardware cost per identity, making mass replication a tough computational walnut to crack. However, this continuous latency tax severely degrades transaction throughput and handicaps honest agents running on standard consumer hardware.
